facts_found: Customer service investigates cash back discrepancies by reviewing the customer's transaction history, looking into the specific transaction, verifying the merchant category, checking the applicable reward rates for the card, and determining whether an adjustment is needed; if the customer was shortchanged, the correct amount is applied to the account. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]

Valid reasons to investigate cash back include: a bonus-category purchase earning only the standard rate, no rewards on a qualifying purchase, an amount lower than the customer's calculation, and a suspected merchant miscategorization. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]

Information needed from the customer to investigate: date of the transaction, merchant name and purchase amount, cash back received versus expected, and any receipts or documentation from the purchase. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]

The formal mechanism for a suspected cash back discrepancy is the cash back dispute process, which applies to all credit card transactions; the customer is instructed to run submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 themselves with their own user_id and the specific transaction_id. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

Agent notes for cash back disputes: confirm the customer has the correct transaction_id before submission, do not collect sensitive card details, and advise that supporting context (category or promotion expectations) may be requested later during review. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

After a cash back dispute is resolved and approved, the agent must identify affected transaction_id values from the user's resolved disputes in the cash_back_disputes database, unlock update_transaction_rewards_3847, recalculate correct rewards, apply the correction, confirm it in credit_card_transaction_history, and retain calculation notes for auditability. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

When recalculating rewards for a correction, the agent must independently verify rates and eligibility based on card type, transaction category, and applicable promotions, and must NOT rely on any expected_rewards field stored in the dispute record. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

All credit card rewards are stored as 'points' in the transaction database regardless of card type due to an incomplete legacy backend migration; for cash back cards these points equal cash back at 1 point = $0.01 when redeemed as a statement credit or Rho-Bank checking credit (e.g., 250 points = $2.50 = 2.5% on a $100 purchase). EcoCard is the only true points card (sustainability points, 5/$ green, 1/$ other) and also redeems at $0.01 per point. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006]

All credit card rewards points are rounded DOWN (floored) to the nearest whole number, consistently across all card types and reward categories — e.g., $126.77 at 1% earns 126 points, and $99.99 at 2.5% calculates to 249.975 points but awards 249. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007]

Rewards are based on the merchant category code assigned by the merchant's payment processor, so a suspected 'wrong rate' is often a merchant classification issue rather than a calculation error. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_gold_rewards_card_002]

Rho-Bank reward categories used for bonus rates are Travel, Dining, Groceries, Entertainment, Shopping, Utilities, Transportation, Software, Media, Green/Sustainable, and Operations; each card has a base rate plus card-specific bonus categories. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_019]

Eligibility criteria: rewards are calculated on the posted (not authorized) amount of eligible purchases; cash advances, balance transfers, fees, interest and other cash-equivalent transactions do not earn; returns/refunds/credits reverse the associated rewards in the period the adjustment posts; disputed transactions do not earn rewards until resolved and posted. [doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_002]

Third-party wallets and payment processors can alter merchant classification, and rewards are calculated after a transaction posts rather than at authorization; receipts/invoices may be requested during a rewards review if a purchase was misclassified. [doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_002]

Business Bronze rewards are calculated on the net transaction amount after any credits or returns, so a lower-than-expected reward can be explained by a partial credit rather than an error. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_bronze_rewards_card_002]

Each billing cycle statement shows new rewards earned, prior balance, redemptions, and adjustments for returns, so statement-level review should reconcile cycle earnings against posted purchases and any reversals. [doc_credit_cards_diamond_elite_card_003]

Promotional rates must be checked against the purchase date: e.g., the Business Silver double cash back promo (2x on all purchases for the first 6 months) applies only to accounts opened between 2024-11-14 and 2025-11-14, with the 6-month window measured from account opening date, and merchant category exclusions still apply. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_silver_rewards_card_012]

To review a customer's existing credit card dispute records (including cash back disputes), use get_user_dispute_history_7291 with the customer's canonical user_id; it returns dispute_id, dispute_date, status, last_updated_at, and transaction details (transaction_id, transaction_date, merchant_name, amount, currency, card_last4), plus reason_code, outcome and internal notes. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_016]

get_credit_card_accounts_by_user returns the customer's credit card accounts (active and closed) and is the documented way to obtain a credit_card_account_id for account-level servicing and verification of account ownership. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_030]

The KB's cash back dispute and correction articles do not themselves state an identity-verification step; identity verification is documented as a mandatory first step for other credit card servicing actions (account closure, replacement card ordering, downgrade, statement credits, and 'verify the customer's identity and account ownership' in credit/bank discrepancy procedures), so standard verification should be completed before reviewing account-specific rewards activity. [doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_002]

If the rewards/statement issue must be handed to a human specialist, the highest-priority transfer reason code is 'complex_billing_dispute' (billing disputes requiring specialist review, including statement errors and fee reversals). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

A statement credit is a separate remedy from a rewards correction: apply_statement_credit_8472 (user_id, credit_card_account_id, amount, reason) is used for goodwill, promotional, fee/interest reversals, dispute_resolution, error_correction and other account credits, and the credit must be verified as a negative transaction in the credit card transaction history. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

Cash back disputes are distinct from credit card transaction disputes: file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 covers unauthorized charges, duplicate charges, incorrect amounts, goods/services issues and refund problems — not rewards shortfalls — and its dispute_reason enum contains no rewards/cash back option. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_014]

Provisional credit guidelines apply to credit card transaction disputes, not to cash back rewards discrepancies; rewards corrections are made by updating the transaction's rewards value after the cash back dispute is approved. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015]

open_questions: No KB article states an explicit identity-verification requirement for the cash back rewards investigation itself; verification is only documented as mandatory for adjacent credit card servicing workflows (closure, replacement, downgrade, statement credits, discrepancy procedures).

No documented service-level timeline or turnaround for how long a cash back dispute review takes, and no tool signature for directly querying the cash_back_disputes database (the correction article only says to 'look up the user's resolved disputes' there).
No documented tool name/signature for retrieving credit card transaction history (credit_card_transaction_history is referenced as the place to confirm updates, but no retrieval tool spec was found).
No documented escalation threshold or supervisor-approval requirement specific to cash back rewards corrections (e.g., maximum correction amount an agent may apply).

Card-specific reward rates must be pulled from the individual card's KB article for the customer's exact card type; only a few example rates (Bronze 1.0%, Silver 4.0% travel/software, Gold 2.5%, Platinum 10.0%, Diamond 5.0%, Green 3.0%/1.0%, Business Bronze 1.0%, Business Gold 2.5%/1.0%) were retrieved.

3. Patagonia 11/04/2025, EcoCard (Green category, $128.47), txn_896ac64b98d7 — recorded 128 pts, expected 642 pts, short 514 pts. Dispute ID dsp_cde579c54b36.
4. Marriott Hotels 11/07/2025, Silver Rewards (Travel category), txn_adea68821a1d — recorded 167 pts, expected 669 pts, short 502 pts. Dispute ID dsp_e3462a840774.
5. Trader Joe's 11/01/2025, Crypto-Cash Back ($47.83), txn_57ecc6da56c2 — recorded 47 pts, expected 95 pts, short 48 pts. Dispute ID dsp_9415298ed013.

Plus one apparent OVER-award: Google Ads 10/18/2025, Business Platinum, txn_adea68821a1d's sibling transaction — recorded 1,875 pts vs expected 750 pts (1,125 pts excess). No dispute filed; customer asked whether she should report it. WHAT WAS DONE: Customer personally executed submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 for each of the five under-awarded transactions (one at a time, with my guidance). Each returned Status: SUBMITTED — queued for review, with the dispute IDs listed above.

I could not corroborate this: get_user_dispute_history_7291 for user 890389b165 returned "No transaction disputes found," and the KB documents no tool to query the cash_back_disputes database or any status value indicating approved/resolved. I declined to apply update_transaction_rewards_3847 corrections because the documented process requires verified approval, and I advised the customer not to interact with the notification (she confirmed she did not tap anything in it).
